Resurrection Pastor

By: Latashia Naidoo | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What happens when a family refuses to let go of their deceased loved one... by not burying him?

Unique Selling Point:
It's divided both the faith community and society in general. Why aren't the family of a man, so revered within the Christian faith, burying him - more than a year after he died?

Summary:
It’s been more than 400 days since Johannesburg pastor Siva Moodley died – allegedly from Covid-
19. To date, he has yet to be buried.
His family and some members of his congregation believe that he will be resurrected. Meanwhile,
his body is still being stored in a freezer at Martin’s Funeral Parlour in Fourways. Since September
2021, no family member has visited the establishment, nor have storage fees been paid.
The matter has now been lodged at the Johannesburg Magistrate Court for the body to be legally
disposed of – but has not yet been set down for hearing.

Further information:
There has been an investigation by The Commission for the Promotion and Protection of the
Rights of Cultural, Religious and Linguistic Communities (CRL Rights Commission) which
determined that they cannot intervene given that this is an interpretation/misinterpretation
of doctrine. They have since referred the matter to the South African Council of Churches.

Press Release:


The Miracle Man

A man of miracles, the heart of his congregation and a firm believer in resurrection, for over twenty years Siva Moodley was a rockstar in his own church. But more than 400 days since his passing, the well-known pastor in Gauteng, has yet to be buried or resurrected. Instead, it’s business as usual in the church, including offers for counselling sessions with the pastor, for a small fee. Inside a funeral home in Johannesburg however, the pastor’s remains, remain unclaimed. Carte Blanche investigates.

Producer: Latashia Naidoo | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


VO:
It’s Sunday morning service at The Miracle Centre in Joburg…

VO:
The seats fill up quickly as dozens of congregants stream into the arena…
eager for the Word…

VO:
The lead pastors take to the stage.. the congregants hanging on their every word…

PAUSE

VO:
But the man whose ministry bears his name…
Is noticeably absent…

VO:
Yet no one at this church will admit to the real reasons ‘why?’...

VO:
Dr Siva Moodley gained fame in his church - and some Christian circles - as a ‘man of miracles…’

VO:
A popular Televangelist and self-styled Apostle…

VO:
… who claimed he could cure cancer, regrow limbs, and even… raise the dead.

VO:
For over 25 years, his larger than life personality, prophetic ministry, and claims of miraculous healings - attracted a global following…

VO:
Then in August last year… he died.

VO:
While some thought that would be the end of his ministry…

Its doors remained open…

With his wife, Jessie, and two children, now leading the flock…

PAUSE


VO:
But that’s not what this story is about… or why we went undercover…

You see, more than a year after his passing, Dr Siva has yet to be laid to rest.

PAUSE

VO:
His family still haven’t publicly acknowledged his death.

… They believe he will be resurrected…

LINK
“This is where Pastor Siva Moodley’s body has remained for the past 435 days… at Martin’s Funeral Parlour in Fourways…
His family claimed the body last August, but have not paid storage fees – or visited – since…
All because: they’re waiting for a miracle.”

VO:
But the people who have been storing his body since his death, have confirmed that Dr Siva remains very dead…

VO:
Tens of thousands of people subscribed to Dr Siva’s brand of ‘prosperity’ gospel - the theology that teaches God rewards faith with monetary wealth.

VO:
At his church, miracles were ‘normal’…

VO:
… as were his beliefs in resurrection…

VO:
The issue has exploded into a controversy that’s not only split his church…

But developed into a social media spat of near Biblical proportions.

VO:
… with many accusing the family of ‘blasphemy’, and making a ‘mockery’ of the Christian Faith.

VO:
Pastor Giet Khosa is chairperson of the International Federation of Christian Churches.

“Look, I can only speculate, but I won;t find anything in the Bible to back up stuff what they’re believing. It’s not in the Bible…”

LINK
“The Bible is the most-read book in the world… it’s also one of the most divisive when it comes to academic versus religious interpretations of Scripture. Which begs the question: is it a question of belief in miracles, or just unresolved grief – that’s preventing Pastor Siva’s family from allowing him to rest in peace?”

CLAIRE:
“You start to think, ‘what is it?’ Is it a belief that a miracle like resurrection will happen in their lives? Or is it another type of loss that they haven’t processed?’

PASTOR KHOSA:
“When you lose someone like that - the pillar of the family, the pillar of the church - it’s quite traumatic, very traumatic, and the pain goes deep.”

VO:
But many have questioned the secrecy behind Dr Siva’s death…
and why, even after his brother confirmed it last year, his social media accounts remain active - as if he were still alive?

VO:
It’s a discussion that’s trended on social media since last August.

VO:
Could it be - as some are suggesting - something more sinister than unresolved grief?

CLAIRE:
“So what are your thoughts on Dr Siva Moodley, who passed away over 400 days ago?

PROF. MARIA
‘As a Biblical scholar and theologian, I don’t see any evidence that he is going to rise again - within the lifetime of his family.’

VO:
Professor Maria Frahm-Arp is head of Religion Studies at the University of Johannesburg.

CLAIRE:
‘What does the Bible say about resurrection?’

PROF. MARIA:
‘The vast majority of people believe that Jesus died and rose again and conquers death… (REMOVE MIDDLE BIT)...
Since the resurrection of Jesus, we haven’t had another person who has risen from the dead.’

VO:
Well that’s not what some ministries would have us believe.

Acts of deception in the clergy aren’t a new phenomenon…

Nor is it the first time that prophetic charismatic leaders in the country have created renewed hope around the seemingly impossible…

VO:
Some have gained notoriety for deliberately deceiving their followers'...

VO:
But the case of Dr Siva’s ‘resurrection’ remains one of the most controversial…

… With many still of the belief that the man who allegedly performed countless miracles … Will defy death…


VO:
Over the past few months, we sent Dr Moodley’s wife Jessie and son David numerous requests for comment…

… over why Dr Siva was not being buried? Allegations of exploiting his memory for financial gain? And the deception surrounding his ‘return’.

Despite all our questions… we were met with silence…

PAUSE

VO:
So we decided to seek out these revelations for ourselves…

Man: ‘The mic is on. Did you ask permission to record?’

VO:
And were confronted by members of the church.

Allison:
‘Of course we are aware that it will be released. We’ve had so many other news articles and stories released without their comment. But we can’t comment or I cannot comment at this point - it’s really up to them. But I will let them know… I have been letting them know so they are aware…”

LINK:
‘Unfortunately, the doors were shut and slammed in our face, and we leave with many unanswered questions.’

VO:
Issues surrounding the burial remain shrouded in secrecy…
With even his siblings in Durban - not associated with the ministry - claiming they too have been kept in the dark…

VO:
Yet while Dr Siva’s beliefs in resurrection power may have influenced the family on this matter - South African law is specific…

VO: … a deceased person ‘can predetermine the manner in which their body will be disposed of…’

VO:
But former congregants say the family are exploiting people’s blind faith with the ‘resurrection’ narrative…

… And that by keeping Dr Siva’s memory alive, they’re keeping their church - and themselves - financially afloat.

VO:
His website still offers one-on-one sessions with the man who's been dead for over 14 months… for a price.

And anyone who comments or asks about this - or his death on social media is immediately blocked.

VO:
Author Cheryl Benadie is a former congregant - who left because she was convinced that the church was a cult…

PAUSE

CLAIRE:
“So why do you think that his wife and his children are continuing with this ‘resurrection’ narrative?’

CHERYL:
“He was kind of the centre of the Universe in their home and their church. And I think that is what they’re still living now. I don’t think that they have an identity outside of him, sadly.”

LINK:
With a growing number of self-proclaimed prophets in Africa who claim they can perform miracles - for a price, many have questioned: are they praying for or praying on people?”

VO:
Many of Dr Siva’s former congregants believe it’s the latter…

His once-mighty ministry has now experienced a fall from grace - having dwindled down from hundreds of congregants each Sunday, to mere handfuls …

VO:
Meanwhile, the Moodley family have still not responded to our requests for an interview…

And the question of what’s to happen to the body, is no longer their decision to make.

VO:
After more than 14 months of storing the body - without payment, the owners of the funeral parlour have now taken the matter to the Johannesburg Magistrates Court -

To legally dispose of the remains…

… of a man, whose decades-long legacy has now been reduced to that of the so-called ‘resurrection pastor’....
